t:
Oh. This is terrible.

But Waterlily does not need to worry... Life is stronger than any sickness. Over the eons of my existence, I have seen so much. Believe me - life always finds a way. Any trials just make it more tenacious. This too will pass like so many other things.

As for Darkness... do not be afraid. Insolent children. I have those, too, unfortunately. Children rebel against their parents, unaware that we do what is best for them.

Oh yeah?

Perhaps we could use this... If Nihaz is a problem for the All-Mother, she might help Sarnaut - the enemy of my enemy is my friend, right?

Try to explain to her that we're on the same side. Yes, we harvest the Ambrosia, but only because we desperately need it, and if those rotten things are a threat to her, we could help her fight them. We have quite an arsenal here, after all.

How is it going? How is it going?! Are you serious?!

I'm sitting at this wrecked base in the forest, trying to figure out what's going on. No apprentices, no amenities, nothing! Even the toilet is not working here, let alone scientific equipment. I'll have to wait for Felix and Ivan to send me replacement parts.

And there are no signs of Herbert and Elena. It's like they vanished into thin air. If they are not with the All-Mother, then I don’t know what to think. Herbert doesn't seem like someone who'd get killed by a wandering stump. And Elena is smarter than she looks.

Yes. There's something. But it's too early to draw conclusions...

Although... What other options are there? In short, I discovered some ruins. It's a whole city, but it's overgrown. It might be thousands of years old - all the metal has long turned to dust. Only the foundations and parts of the walls remain.

I guess your friends had nothing to do with it. I doubt they'd build with stone, which means... there was another civilization here. I need to find out what happened to it.

Here I'm going to say my goodbyes and this: you don't have much time - Felix and Ivan are chomping at the bit, they need the Ambrosia, and your Children won't let our harvesters into the forest. They want you to talk to the All-Mother about harvesting it.

That's all. Goodbye.
Come in! Do you copy? I repeat. Do you copy? Can you hear me? Tep take this rusty thing! Do you copy? Come in!

January 9, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's notes.

We started researching the local flora. I compared the samples collected at the main base and here. The difference is visible to the naked eye. It seems that the flora at the Gates very quickly acquired the properties necessary for defense and even offense. It is quite curious that the plants seem to interact with each other, as if trying to work out a "single tactic" against us.

January 15, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's notes.

I was able to trace certain successive changes. It seems that local plants develop a certain specialization fairly quickly. Completely different ways of fighting against the Mechanoids, Humans, Aoidoi, Arisen. In the first case, plants develop corrosive properties that attack metals. In the second case, intense biogenic erosion occurs. In the third case, the development of toxicity. In the fourth - accelerated putrefaction.

It seems that the plants around the Penelope have also begun to react to our presence, but fortunately, it's noticeably weaker.

February 1, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's notes.

An interesting discovery - we managed to find reduced defense elements on plants around the base.  It seems that some time (probably quite significant) ago, these plants already faced some kind of threat, and after repelling it, they completely lost their properties over several generations.

This needs to be verified. I have a suspicion that the forest around us, for the most part, just wants us to "leave" and not "die in terrible agony." Related to this is the spread of an unusually allergenic pollen that caused massive hay sickness among Penelope employees.

Our next task is to collect new samples during the active spore dispersal phase.
These are notes from the first report

January 5, 1022. Elena Zimina's Notes.

I want to try and confirm or refute the theory that the animals began to react more aggressively to our presence as soon as we began to extract the Ambrosia more actively. I will go further into the forest to see how animals behave in their usual environment.

January 25, 1022. Elena Zimina's Notes.

Incredible! I was able to obtain extremely valuable information. Animals and birds are fundamentally different in their behavior at a distance from the base. They behave more peacefully, almost without interacting with each other. At the same time, near the base they change their way of life - they breed many times more intensively, predators barely touch herbivores, and they all try to get inside the perimeter.

February 5, 1022. Elena Zimina's Notes.

Important observation: Over the past month, there has been an increase in local animal activity around the Penelope. It seems that the ecosystem is being restructured - the changes are similar to those that occurred near the Bare Ground.

I think there is a center where local animals and plants get the impulse to change their behavior. Hence the conclusion: there's some kind of intelligence out there that is set against us.

We need to take measures to reduce the number of animals around the Penelope, otherwise soon we'll be overrun.
These are notes from the second report

January 4, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's and Elena Zimina's notes.

When we arrived at the Penelope, we discovered a qualitatively different level of interaction between the organisms of Eden. Unfortunately, on the Bare Ground we started observing the flora and fauna too late. We have our own theory about the unity of the flora and fauna of Eden, but we need to do independent research. It was decided that Herbert would take on the flora, and Elena the fauna. Each of us will write a report, and then we will try to bring our observations together.

January 31, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's and Elena Zimina's notes.

Our observations confirm the following: normally the animals and flora of Eden do not differ from their counterparts from Sarnaut (except here all animals have plant features in their structure, which is a consequence of their completely different origin). However, in a stressful situation - such as the massive deforestation we just carried out, the entire population of organisms undergoes a complete restructuring, and begins to work in a much greater symbiosis, becoming like an army.

The issue of transmitting a signal that allows them to coordinate their actions remains open. At first we thought that telepathy was taking place here, but our mystic on duty, Yolanda, claims these animals and plants do not transmit any thoughts.

February 13, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's and Elena Zimina's notes.

Amazing discovery! It seems that we managed to find the source of signals that animals and plants are exchanging - it's the roots. The roots of the Great Tree which is the heart of this forest. The roots densely permeate the soil and therefore can easily bind different types of creatures together. Local animals have special receptors on their feet that can read information from sprouts that come to the surface.

We managed to find special nodes, which are like centers where signals from the surrounding forest are collected. Each of these nodes is protected by special thorns that attack from the ground. They are like some kind of brains that coordinate the attacks of the thorns.

According to our observations, every day the thorns become harder and sharper. New samples are required to compare and confirm the hypothesis.
These are notes from the third report

Herbert de Vevre, hah! I know him by another name, and we'd known each other long before you and Skulnar were born. The man is smarter than he looks.

Elena is no slouch either, so if this couple found something here and wrote about it, it would be the truth.

But where are they? Something tells me there were some aborigines here.

The locals don't look like weasels. I'm sure they can be trusted.

If it gets violent, don't worry. You'll get a huge monument on the Upper City's central square.

Take your friends and go there. In the meantime, I'll finish what Herbert and Elena started. I suspect that they were on the verge of a great discovery.

Get the locals to trust you. Learn who they are, what the want, what their priorities in life are... come up with a way to manipulate them into doing our thing. First of all, we need the ambrosia.

If you come across a goddess, try to reason with her. Nihaz is our common enemy, after all.

If you find something interesting, report to me immediately. Oh yes, and try to find Herbert, Elena, and the others from the base. If they're alive, of course.
I'll give you a holographic transmitter. I want you to call me as often as you can and report your latest findings.
Here. Try not to break or lose it.
Come in! Do you copy? As you can see, this is a multipurpose device for long distance communication.

Who hath the Word to speak, let him speak!

All we do is defend ourselves. Do you wish to speak?

We are children of All-Mother, living in the blessed land of Eden. Apparently, you are Children of Sarn. I see it in you. It's amazing! Sarn has long been considered lost. I also see darkness. What a weird mixture...

All-Mother wanted me to find you. She's been talking with you through her creatures, but you didn't hear. Now that we've learned your language, we can talk. Others didn't understand it, no matter how hard they tried. It is hard to fill a cup which is already full. But yours is empty.
To come with me. All-Mother wants me to take you to the Great Tree. We will talk there. It is not the time for words. It is time to go. Let's not waste it. Do the right thing. All-Mother awaits.
Everything in the Universe has its beginning and end.
Whew, I thought we were dead, hah.

Not that much of justice, to be honest. Ugh, them gods... all they can is make up tangled rules and punish sinners. Is it our fault that there's immortality in Sarnaut? Have we been asking for it? They forced me to drink dragon's blood, did you know that? Whatev. They're the bosses, like the Kanians say, hah. Let's try to figure out whether they can help us.
I admit, you've been lucky in trials lately.

I'm getting more and more convinced that we should stay away from the gods. Do we really want to drag that lady to Sarnaut to straighten things up by her own rules? I don't think that anyone's going to be happy about it. On the other hand, it might be not as bad as we think. She could have thrown the trial to impress her own followers. Let's see how she will act.
It's pretty nice around here. I like it.
I can't help wondering if there are any rules left that you haven't broken.
I've been watching you, listening to your talks, seeing your deeds. Trust me, I know enough. Most of what you deem important is, in fact, minor. All in due time. Sooner or later, you will understand.
The old tribe did a lot of evil to our Forest. Even your Expedition is less dangerous than those who neglected All-Mother's wisdom and surrendered to Darkness.

I trust my sister. She believes that you're the one that will save our world. Rhubarb and others are blind, but All-Mother has spoken to Waterlily. She has chosen you among others. There is something in you, after all.

Aliens! Have you been invited to our world? You had one of your own, and you managed to break it to pieces! You ruined your own Creator! Darkness, Light, Order, and Chaos are mixed in you! Now you're chopping down our forests, killing our animals, poisoning our land! Tell me why you should be treated differently?
It's good to see you even outside Sarnaut!

Only a few Sparks could leave Sarnaut. However, it happens more and more often since the Seals were destroyed. Those whose time has come, leave our world and travel across the Universe. I ended up here, in Eden.

Just one. He's angry and insane. I had no idea that someone can be so consumed by hatred. He's powerless now. His Spark has gone out. All he can is be a cool shadow, scaring the guts out of locals. He has last been seen in the Rotten Forest.
All-Mother is wise, but I'm afraid of the Darkness that has come to our world. Are you offering help? We should use it.

I believe that everything happens for a reason. You are here, in our world, for a reason. Even though you've done more harm than good, you might eventually defeat the Darkness that has come to Eden. We've never had to face anything like it. It means that we need someone we've never met before to fight it.
Our Forest has seen a lot of hardship, and you're part of it.

It's impossible until you stop chopping down our trees. You have no right to steal things from our world and bring them into yours! Can't you see that all living things are suffering? There's only dying land where you chopped down the trees.

Father was right, this IS the world of gods!

Father... I can't believe that he's gone. Will I ever see him again?

I understand you have your doubts about me, but I re-estimated my priorities.

We need to understand what's going on here. This is a strange world but we might find the key to saving Sarnaut here. Yes, I care about our world too. I want it to stay the way it is. After all, I need a place to play my little games, right?
This... is... amazing! Here, in this world... I can breathe!

I don't think, I act! Let's blow something up, okay?

So many new impressions! So many new ideas! It's time to do something! My hands are itching! I need to create! Ooooh, just give me a workshop and a heap of nuts and bolts! I know I can come up with something! Just look at all the saws lying around! Imagination running wild!

Come on, go and find Catherina! Tell her I'm ready for action!
Woah, look at all these new constructions! I wonder where they found the time for it.

Still searching for the love of my life. Although it's just a tiny adventure for you, one of many, you might remember that we met before. On Gipat.

I was the dragon resistance leader, trying to disrupt the idiotic show. I'm sure you understand my motives better now. You know I was right!

Let me tell you one more secret. I was also one of Sarn's cultists. I hoped that he helps me find the love of my life.

There's no point in telling you the rest of the story. I haven't found what I've been looking for, and Sarn... well, you know.

But if the Spark isn't in Sarnaut, where can it be? I gave it a very good thought. Of course, there's the concept of "Heaven" in many religions, where all dead people go... But I had my doubts until I found out where all the Sparks go after leaving Sarnaut. You know where? To the world that can be safely called "Heaven."

Eden has been my destination ever since. Luckily, Klavdia sought our help. I took some of the cultists, the ones I knew well, and here we are.

Alas, our search is slow. Why? You will see... soon.

Ask me if you need teleportation or mailing services. We can set up steady connection with Sarnaut when you arrive.
Greetings in the new world! This is the true heaven.

Quite well, thank you. Did I say, "quite well?" Absolutely perfect!

Too perfect, in fact. This world... how should I put it... is unusual. One thing you ought to remember: the Purgatory, Servants of Tensess, and the lay brother, they're all in Sarnaut. There are no such things here. Death here is permanent.

Thankfully, it's not that easy to die here. There was this knucklehead, stupid enough to reach out to grab something from under a running saw. Lost his arm in a second. I thought he was done with. You know what happened? He regrew a working limb! Over a week's time!

But that's not all! Then wild beasts came, and one of the guys lost his head.

You won't believe it either. He regrew the head! As good as new. Blank memory, of course, but it's nothing, really.

I had a cripple leg back on Sarnaut. It hurt like hell. It hurt so bad that I had to take psy-spice to kill the pain. Guess what? The pain is gone! I can run a thousand in this world!

We have to soak the Arisen in formaldehyde. Otherwise they risk becoming normal people, hehe. On the other hand, old wounds remain unchanged.

But don't worry, there are reliable ways to die even here. For example, if you're poisoned or ripped to pieces. We've lost a lot of our guys. Be careful with local creatures.
Greetings. What seems to be the problem? Headache? Diarrhea? Shaky hands?

Oh, nice.

Where did we last meet? On Irene? On Ammer? On Ferris?

No, I've never been on Irene.

This place is more fun. For the first time in my life I can have everything I want. There's no control of spare parts, you just grab what you want. We've got tons of them here. I can assemble any mechanoid to your liking! Oh, and there's ambrosia. Cool stuff. There's no limit to the power of my engines.

I don't think we're anywhere near discovering all its properties. We might be on the threshold of a great breakthrough!

Uh, I don't even know what to say.

Do you know how I landed here? Of course, you don't. You know how many Great Tree specialists there are in Sarnaut? That's right, not so many.

When they ordered me to quit my job and go to Suslanger, I got upset. And the things that we're doing here, ugh...

This is the new world, absolutely unique, full of secrets to explore... but all we want is ambrosia.

We chop down trees, we pick up branches and leaves. We produce wood as well. Everything is crushed and pressed. We squeeze out juice and steam it. This is how we get concentrated ambrosia, much more powerful than the stuff from Suslanger.

Ambrosia. The blood of Great Trees...

I dreamed of knowing where it all began.

And now I'm having a hand in the destruction of this world...

Haha, I never expected to be here! But the pay is great, not to mention all the handsome males in uniforms! The military are the sexiest. And the most appealing of all is our commander Felix. All covered in scars... so manly!

They say it was Gorluxor who beat him, when Yasker and Felix were trying to trap the old Great Mage. But you know, they may be lying.

I had a fussier job before. I had so much "oooh" and "aaaah" during the day and so much bathhouse during the night...

This place is quiet for a change. I can talk to girls all I want or have as many tea breaks as I like. It's just these animals behind the wall. They're real scary.

Welcome to Eden. You're outside Sarnaut. Keep that in mind while you're here. This world is dangerous. Every creature outside this base is dangerous, be it an animal, a bird, or a plant. The local population is also extremely aggressive. They hated us at the first sight... and we hated them. Beware of the savages with arrows. We don't have the Purgatory here, there's no Servant of Tensess to resurrect you. If you're dead, you're dead. No matter how much I want everyone to return home safely, I know that many will have to stay here for the eternity.

What do we do in the current situation? A long-range recon, of course. We need to know what forces the locals have, where they main cities lie. We'll know then where to strike. To do it, we need a small group. Three people, five tops. You can make a great leader for the recon party.

If we don't do it, we risk losing the initiative. The animals' attacks get more and more massive and powerful. They're wary about approaching the base, but it's only a matter of time. Although they use primitive weapons, their power is in numbers.

Here's my solution: either they stop attacking us or we'll kick them back into the swamp they crawled out of.

We're here for ambrosia. The price for ambrosia is over ten thousand crystals per pound. It pays for the whole Expedition, which is quite expensive, I must say. It pays both for Catherina's research and for the search of... whoever we're looking for. Some goddess or something. The local savages are putting the entire operation at risk. As if mad beasts and plants weren't enough! I want you to help us work out a diplomatic solution and avoid war.

So far, all out attempts to communicate with the locals were futile. We tried, we really tried talking, we even tried to trade. They simply hate the guts of our campaign. Did Klavdia expect us to find allies here? She was wrong.

Not to mention the mysterious goddess we're looking for. At this point, I think it's just a myth. We haven't come across a single god here. Just the mad beasts, mad plants, and mad locals...

You might get through to them. I'd hate for another war to begin. It's crazy expensive. Our main focus is on gathering ambrosia and sending it back to Sarnaut. You'll have to walk the extra mile... and every mile in between.

Haven't I already told you that I do not wish to see you here? We were preparing for this expedition for a year. We calculated every step. Look at what you and Klavdia have done! Turned up here out of the blue! You were told to wait! Why couldn't you just be patient? Look around you. This world is completely different from others. We have no idea by what laws it is living. Of course, we had to get into trouble with these wild mud-diggers. How were we supposed to know that they'd hate us the moment they see us? I've never seen anyone so dim! Not even in the darkest corners of Umoir! I really don't think that you can do anything about them. Knowing your problem-solving skills, I assume the effect will be opposite.

Klavdia misled us, to put it mildly. "Here you will find the key to the victory over Nihaz," she said. "Find my Mother, she will be your ally," she said. We found no one! Even if we find her, there's no guarantee that she'll be any friendlier than the locals.

The only good thing here is ambrosia. This is the key to progress and development. I'm sure it will be the straw that will break Nihaz's back.

Since you're here, I need to keep you busy. There's the other base, Penelope. We've lost connection a while ago. We need to figure out why. As soon as we finish the ongoing things, you and I will go there.
You never learned to listen to me and obey, did you?

I loved it! Hah!

I wish my guys from the Landfill could lay their hands on these magnificent machines! They'd set them right in order! They'd travel across the desert and get on the Worm's nerves, making him spit out the rare ancient junk that your lot is hunting for.

I could get one for Fury as a gift...
Don't come close. I need a break.
I am not setting foot in this pathetic wreck ever again. This would have never happened if harvesters were made on Umoir. Shame!
Your destructive tendencies scare me. Is this the foundation Sarn laid when he created you?

Dear child, if I imposed my vision on all the worlds, would we have the diversity Verbena must have told you about? When mortals choose their path, I do not interfere...

I have no power to destroy what is created. I am a creator, not a destroyer.

Your immortality primarily harms you. I could heal you... but you don't want that. So be it.

Well, that suits me just fine.

Actually, it's what we initially wanted.

I just need to be sure that she won't try to impose her rules on anyone when she comes into our world. Otherwise, I'm not ready to give up technology at the behest of some goddess, even if she wants the best for everyone.

"Has a shard of Sarn in her" - what is she trying to say? What?!

quests: We are all part of the cycle of life

t:
I couldn't have done this without you, "Hero of Sarnaut".

Want to know what's next?
Empty threats. Try to stay alive for a start.

Now I'll say goodbye. I have other matters to attend to - like this interesting little world I've been observing. And I'll be taking my demons with me.

I have plenty of time left, and you... you stay here. Perhaps we will meet again in a few thousand years. I'm curious to see what you will have achieved by then.
Well, shall we speak? I'm going to make quite a few changes...

Don't be so testy!

Yes, the events that are taking place are very dramatic. However, you and I are in the same boat now.

So... Sarnaut. A poor little world split into pieces, with a deity trapped inside. Inhabited by very quarrelsome races, and most of them are natural-born destroyers.

So what do we do with it?

Well, for starters, I will become the absolute ruler of your world. Everyone must obey me. Really, it's such a small thing. To control my future subjects, I will need an army, and fortunately you have already assembled one of those. Yes, yes, I'm talking about that army of the undead that stormed the Citadel. I'll take it, thank you for this generous gift.

Besides, as you already know, I don't really like it when someone dies. Now no one will die. This is the Gift of Hirkalla, which will replace the Gift of Tensess, or rather the Gift of Nihaz. Perhaps we will also bring back all those who died - existing as Sparks in a box doesn't sound very exciting, if you ask me. I will think of a job for those souls.

Of course, such a population will require a lot of space. I'm going to restore your little world from separate allods into something whole. Of course, it won't be easy, and I'll need the help of these Great Mages of yours.

And finally, we will destroy all these gods - the All-Mother's parasites. They're out there somewhere, waging an endless war. But I'm sure they don't stand a chance against you, the people of Sarnaut.

You and I are in the same situation. I don't know any more than you do. We are at the point where my journey began. Here Klavdia decided to become Alice to try and fix everything. As you can see, I failed.
We have hope. I don't want to rely on luck too much. Luck is a fickle lady, and fate is unfair. Hope is all we have left.

My sister will set her plan into motion. Maybe you'll even like it?

I'm afraid things aren't going so well. Death and afterlife are important parts of life, the All-Mother and even the mad Kyros are both right about that. So we should expect... consequences. We can minimize them.

However, few people trust you now. And... me.

We can only wait.

Right now we can't do anything about Hirkalla. But... perhaps later we'll get our chance. Because a twist of fate can change everything, so who knows... what might happen?

Child of Sarn, I see that you care about the needs of my Children.

I'm starting to understand what my daughter wanted from you. Well, you helped me, and I see no reason to refuse your request.

The expedition believes in the power of their machines, in the creations of a rational mind, but remember: in Eden every creature has a soul, and life will always find a way. In a moment of great danger, this world will save itself.

Well, we really stepped into it. And everything was going so well: there's a truce between the Empire and the League, and we're fighting Nihaz together...

But no, even if we win now, things won't be the same.

War will probably break out again, perhaps between other groups. Like the Orcs and Gibberlings against Zem and Elves, heh.

The most important advice is to survive. So don't go asking for trouble. Although... We'll probably end up in deep sh... Well, you know.

If we survive, I'm going to head home. Why? So many orcs unsupervised - who knows what they'll cook up this time. So no more adventures, I'm going to stay home.

Waterlily has already told us about your troubles, although only rumors have reached us until now.

Yes, this Expedition, which comes from the same world as you, poses a considerable danger.

I agree that we should all work together. The tribes of Eden will unite to fight the outlanders.

However, you must understand that we don't have warriors, only hunters.

We organize trainings. The warriors of your tribe will train the warriors of our tribes.

Alas, if they come to us, your lands will be left without defenders. If you can replace them for a while, then we can finish this training sooner.

To do this, complete the tasks given to you by Camelia, Sumac, and Elm.

quests: Making Friends with Grass and Trees

t: Outlander! There hasn't been anyone like you in Eden for thousands of years!
The Children of Sarn came to our world in an hour of great need.

Yes, we will answer your call!

We will bring not just the warriors of our tribes, but also members of those who live in other parts of our world. Everything is in motion, stories and songs about what is happening here are shared throughout Eden, and the Children are ready to throw the invaders out of this world!

Although there are many strange machines on their side, Eden itself is on ours. The Children are fearless and not afraid of death.

So the time has come. We'll go to our tribes and summon those who have arrived!

The invaders believed that this land will submit to them, but we will that we can protect our world!

Report our decision to Waterlily.
The All-Mother sees everything. She warned us that you would come.

I think that... when this operation was initially planned, a mistake was made. We thought Catherina had become wiser, but she is still the same as she was when she started that madness on Umoir. But Klavdia made the biggest mistake. We consider her almost infallible but as it turns out, she can't be trusted either.

The only one who is able to think sensibly in this situation is Zayan.

My father was wary of him for a reason. Even with all his experience and power, Elleken is in many ways inferior to the great Historian.

I don't really understand the Children's plan yet. We have no commanders, and it looks like the plan is to rely on numbers to overwhelm the enemy. But the base is well-defended and it won't be easy to break through the perimeter, as you've seen earlier.

We can only hope - and I think the scouts confirm this - that our enemies will be even more stupid and will attack first.

When the Expedition arrived at Eden, we began to change. The Children who were once hunters have become warriors, our animals have grown powerful fangs, and our flowers have sprouted thorns.

Other tribes are still peaceful. Living far from the Valley, they do not know troubles and sorrows. They did not deal with the deadly machines and the reanimated bodies of the Old Tribe.

So enlisting their help is not enough. You need to train them.

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

t:
Waterlily has already volunteered to help spread the word to our closest neighbors.

I believe their representatives will arrive here soon. You'll need to talk to Waterlily and then get the other tribal leaders to join us in our fight against the Expedition.

Yes, that's right.

The tribes Evergreen, Deciduous, and Blooming. Their Great Trees are located to the west, north, and east of our Valley. News of what is happening here has already reached them. However, it won't be easy to persuade them to join us.

At my request, they arrived at the agreed meeting place. I guess they would like to talk to you.

It is your example that can inspire other tribes as much as it did us.

Try to convince them.

Yes, our warriors have trained many hunters from other tribes. Now they are ready to fight the Expedition.

Although there are many strange machines on their side, Eden itself is on ours. The Children are fearless and not afraid of death.

We need to know whether they will come to our call when the battle begins!

Go to the leaders and speak with them. We must know the numbers we're going to get in the future battle.

Good news! We have every chance to drive the Expedition out of the Valley.

We are preparing for the final attack, but apparently our enemies are doing the same. The decisive battle is about to begin, and we must be ready.

No, our warriors haven't finished training the other tribes yet.

If you can help us defend the Valley, more warriors can go on this mission. Complete the tasks of Camellia, Sumac, and Elm. By doing this, you will significantly speed up the training of our army.

Ah, Herbert made up his mind after all. I also think we're done here. The natives are extremely hostile, and Felix with his soldiery is not the company I want to keep.

We could visit one of the other worlds on the Star Trail... It would be so romantic!

We need one of those codes that are changed daily to activate the Gates... One that would get us onto the Star Trail.

Of course, no one will give it to you, but it looks like our crafty and cunning Priden managed to get the password. I'd ask him myself, but it would be too suspicious. But no one would suspect you.
I always felt like our adventures would eventually take us to a place we wouldn't be able to get out of.
Not bad, though we really didn't expect to go to war when we mounted a scientific expedition. If I'd known, I would've brought a few extra things with me.

I've been thinking about how we can win this, and I may have a solution.

Our resources are incomparable with what the natives have. However, we have a serious advantage - our determination and willingness to make any sacrifices.

We also have our technology.

Imperial engineers once created a unique weapon - a mana bomb. It's good but not powerful enough to secure us a victory.

But the Ambrosia... its power is unimaginable. We can combine our technologies and the resources of this world, and then no one will stand in our way.

Science division, as you know, is headed by Catherina.

She didn't like the idea at first, but I managed to persuade her. Now your task is to help her create this device.

And my task will be to deliver it to the enemy.

Hmm, indeed...

Well, since you're here, let's talk about it.

Felix is a madman, a military sociopath willing to burn everything down. But you… I honestly thought you were different.

What you are about to do... it's a crime, pure and simple!

What will be the cost of this victory? If we do this, are we any better than Nihaz? He also destroys worlds for the purposes we don't even understand...

Well, if that's your decision, then so be it. But I want no part of this. I have a proposition - you will let us leave Eden, and I will give you the component. Everything that happens after that will be on your conscience.

Yes, I know Felix implemented high-security protocols, but Elena seems to have an idea. Speak with her.

Murk is an old friend. He is true to himself, and I respect that. As for you...

I hope we will all meet again under much better circumstances. Once again, I don't approve of your plan - though perhaps we shouldn't have come to Eden at all...
Here. And be far away when it does its thing. And now goodbye. Soon Elena and I will leave Eden.
Yes, I did not expect this when I agreed to visit this world.

Actually she didn't even care about us - she was laser-focused on you. So when the panic among my colleagues subsided, Elena and I were able to get everyone to the Gates base.

We're helping Catherina with her research of Eden.

Hello there, chief! I've always wanted to blow everything up, yeah. You and Catherina have interesting ideas! I love it!

Well, I'll do it. I'll build you a mana bomb in a couple of days, if need be...

But the Ambrosia part - now there's a problem.

In short, we need this crystalline concentrate... But this is not Suslanger, there are no crystals here. So we need to distill liquid Ambrosia into crystalline form - and this requires time and a lot of this liquid Ambrosia.

And that's another problem. Those Children are vicious. They don't let us collect the Ambrosia. They're hitting us on all fronts, yeah.

If you want Ambrosia to flow through the pipeline, then you must inspire the soldiers with your own example. How?

Complete a few of my tasks, and we'll win, you'll see. As soon as everything is ready, come see me.

By the way, lest you think I'm sitting around twiddling my thumbs here - you'll be able to see the progress yourself. The more you do, the sooner it will be finished.

Yes, chief. Almost everything is ready, but... one component is missing. Yes, that always seems to be the case.

True, but this time I know who has it. After all, we have cameras all over the place, so no one can get through undetected.

If they had worked at Gates-3, then no Alice would have been able to steal the Chronophone, and you wouldn't have had to wallow in the desert.

The component was taken by this elf, Herbert. Maybe he needed it for something, or maybe he is some kind of saboteur, yeah. Ask him to return it.

Without this part, no big boom is gonna happen.
Great, chief! This is exactly what we need! It’s good that you did it quickly, because I’m being rushed here, too.

Come on, chief, I need more Ambrosia. I'm telling you - if you want Ambrosia to flow through the pipeline, then you need to inspire the soldiers with your own example. Complete my tasks, and we'll win.

Ambrosia Mana Bomb or A.M.B.Rosia Project? Well, it's an interesting idea.

I hear the Children told you about a world where people invented a weapon that splits the very essence of matter, causing monstrous damage.

"A.M.B. Rosia" will probably be something similar.

The principle here is simple: we close the energy circuits of an ordinary mana bomb to a concentrate in the crystal form, and the explosion starts a chain reaction with the gradual transformation of matter into energy.

We didn't have enough engineers here to work with mana bombs - when I formed the Expedition, I recruited those who would build Ambrosia mining mechanisms, not weapons, you know...

However, it turns out that you did us a favor when you dragged that goblin Nogrom Junior here. He's supposedly a specialist in explosives.

And although I worry he'll blow up our base before he builds anything, I think it's worth giving him a chance under the circumstances.

Find out what exactly he needs to get it done.

All right, let's start from the beginning. To see what we want to achieve, you need to understand how it all started.

Six years ago we made Sarn and the Architect clash. It was an incredibly risky move but for the first time ever Sarnaut was free from cheeky and destructive gods. At least, that's how it seemed to me.

But Daddy did find a way to ruin our lives. Maverick made Kyros try to get rid of your Immortality. It's only natural that he lost but this wasn't the end.

I suspect that they needed all that for distraction. Nihaz's real target was the Well of Souls. He used it to return to Sarnaut, and I think he affected all newborn Aoidoi. Including Cosmos, who now plays his own games...

Then there was Sogot. Remember how the God of Darkness was trying to get into your head? Skulnar helped you fight it and break the connection. Back in the day, it caused me a great deal of effort to resist it.

What was next? Doomsday predictions? A journey beyond the horizon? You know, even I believed that it was inevitable. But now we have a chance to avoid such future.

So, I've got a plan how to fix everything. You see, Nihaz only looks scary. Everyone trusts his "Boo! I'm the evil God of Darkness! Fear me!" But in fact, he never risked facing an equal. All he's capable of is to pit his enemies against each other and then finish the survivor.

I was his loyal student. We made Sarn and the Architect annihilate one another. Nihaz is a whole different story. He's a harder nut to crack. He will never face us in a battle. But as they say in one of the worlds, the only weapon against a dragon is your own dragon.

We need our own divine patron. You might say that one would be just as bad as the other, or even worse... You're right. The gods you have had to face weren't very nice. But there is one god that will be happy to help us out.

My mother. Surprise-surprise, I also had a mom! In fact, despite the fact that I was Nihaz's step-daughter, I had a full set of real parents. I might have made my mother unhappy at some point, but since she's been at war with Nihaz longer than us, I'm sure we can find common ground.

I thought about her and decided to act. It was too easy to tip you off at Nihaz's Citadel. Cosmos played right into my hands, too. We gathered the army of the dead. Your next task was to distract Nihaz while I was dismantling the fortress to get the coordinates of my mother's world.

You see, she's been hiding out in her own world. She doesn't want to see anyone except her own creations. Nihaz had been looking for her world for years, and he might have found it in the end. He can't enter it but I'm sure his minions are already there.

I can't get in there either: I'm tied to Sarnaut and can't leave it. Moreover, the only Sarnaut's Star Gates have turned to stardust after the epic battle between Sarn and the Architect. I had to kick out both League and Empire and begin building my own Gates.

I've been on the lookout for Nihaz when this lady came by. Alice. She was messing with us. Thankfully, she decided to leave at some point. But as a result, this world got ambrosia, and Catherina and the others got the bit between the teeth. They wanted ambrosia more than anything in the world. And they got it into their heads that it was spilled from my mother's world.

Catherina didn't listen to me. She wanted her own Expedition. Of course, I could break up with her completely, hide Suslanger behind the veil of secret, and don't let anyone near the Gates... but I decided against it. Perhaps, that's what Nihaz wanted. I knew better.

I let them enter mother's world after infiltrating several loyal people in their Expedition. Sarn's former cultists, hehe. They really wanted to believe that my mother was capable of resurrecting their late god.

I was hoping that even if Catherina, Felix, and Ivan would fail, my people could at least deliver a note to my mother.

Something went wrong... Skulnar told me that after wandering along the Star Trail for a while they eventually managed to find the right world. They started building a base, and our unique friend returned together with a small group. Skulnar passed me Catherina's message: they'll be sending news every once in a while.

It's been several months now. There are no news. Whatsoever.

I need your help again.

Catherina was really reluctant to let you join the Expedition. Maybe she was superstitious, or maybe she believed in the Horizon prophecies too much. Remember what unthinkable disaster they promised after the demons set sail outside Sarnaut? You were supposed to perish after setting foot on their ship.

What a load of nonsense. We don't even have ships. Nevertheless, Catherina was strongly against demons and namely you in her Expedition. Well, I listened to her back then. This time, I'm going to do it my way.

I got you a dream team of your friends. Skulnar, Murk, Nogrom... and Eurial. Oh, quit staring. She's useful. Besides, Zayan really straightened her out. She's our loyal ally now, and she knows a lot about my Daddy's doings.

Your task is to follow Catherina's footsteps, find my mother's world, find out what happened to the Expedition, and persuade my mother to become Sarnaut's patron.

And... well... I must admit that I miss her. Tell her that as well.

We were prepared to leave. I gathered everyone, found the right keys, prepared everything... and unleashed an avalanche!

The word about our journey quickly spread among those, who tried to capture the Star Gates in the Dead City. Namely, the Wormfaces from mountain caves, demons, cheated by Catherina, and Draconids... who cause the most problems.

Shortly before your arrival the power went out. The thing is, Draconids captured the local mana station and caused the outage.

I expect it to get even worse. Go now, or it will never happen. League and Imperial fleets are fighting a demonic onslaught near Suslanger but new demons keep arriving. From all Astral...

Here's what you need to do: enter the mana station and figure out why it stopped working. Besides, as Skulnar has been behind the Gates and seen what it's like, we need to get hazmat suits stat. No, assault shells won't work in these conditions. You can find equipment crates all over the camp. Unfortunately, most of the equipment didn't survive this mess. Try searching the boxes. We need half a dozen of suits. Backup won't hurt.
Hi! I can teleport you back to Great Mage Simon in the East. I'm also offering fresh water.
Cheeky. But what choice have we got? That Great Mage caught us in a weak position. It's not that we had that much of a choice here. Keep an eye on him, he can pull some trick.
Hello, hello! We're getting ready for the new attack. My fellows can rip anyone apart! But to tell you the truth, the battles are getting boring. I wish Eladia finished her monstrosity faster.

Aho, frrriend! It's been a harrrd day. Worrrmfaces, scalies, and demons are crrrawling from all corners. Attack after attack, without any breathers. We had to leave the old camp behind and retrrrreat to the Gates, and the ginger-hairrred witch still can't get her machine rrrunning! These are dark times, I swearrr by the tip of my tail.
What do you want from me, little hero? Speak with the elf. Let's see what destiny the Great Mages have in store for the world this time.

As I said, all I need is to enter the Gates. You let me and Sturegga pass, we can keep you company until we reach your destination, and then we'll say our goodbyes. You can keep Skulnar.

Besides, our Draconids will help you defend the Gates from other races, trying to break out of Sarnaut.
Ugh, last time the first leap took us to a different place. Come on, instinct, don't let me down! I don't want to wander forever!
Sure thing. Eladia gave me a special stone for that. Good stuff. What you got? Ah, never mind. Take care. Are you flying?
Um, let me see... ah, here it is.
Congratulations on your first step along the Star Trail. As you know, this is a crowded place. Here we can see the consequences of one of the encounters.

It was a good call to take the Sculptor with us. He's part of a higher Architect. He could easily control the ones we see.

However, Klavdia thinks that if we perish too, the Sculptor will be Sarnaut's only chance against Nihaz. He's her bargaining chip.
Woah! Just look around! How beautiful! While you're getting ready, I'll make some calculations for the future journeys. Maybe, Skulnar won't have to jump back and forth.
You're too weak, Mortals! You can't even survive in the void! Dragons do not fear endless darkness or vacuum.
It looks like there's been a great war on this Trail. It's way older than our world. Perhaps, even older than the rest of the worlds.
See those ruins over there? I dread to imagine a weapon that destroyed it.

Here's the thing... We have five crystals. They must be activated in the correct order to open the portal. We sealed it ourselves, hah. We even left an instruction! But I forgot the order anyway... Can you help?

Uh, you see, we wrote it in a way so only a Sarnaut dweller would understand. It mentions only the latest events, hah. The problem is that I wasn't an eye-witness, so I can't judge. I completely missed the Gods versus Fartitects fight. Here's what it says:

We learned the truth about the Light,

That Demons aren't Sarnaut's blight.

The God of Darkness got a new foe:

Threat under mountains and snow.

Walked along Nezeb's sandy path.

You're still here with us? You can reveal it, it's no high-school math.
Yeah, I figured. You jump into the portal. I'll hang around a little longer. Talk later! It's just too beautiful.
Um... there's something wrong here. We should have put down the answers.
We reached all internal worlds. Everything as Nihaz predicted.
Oh, father, you were such a good student of Nihaz! Your plans are too complex to understand what you really want.
Oh, wow! And the beasts. Oh, and the Gates too. Can you distract them while I'm finding the spare parts?
Dragons of the Void... the Ancients. I heard about them when I was a dragonling. They were our ancestors. The essence of destruction.
Ah, here you are. I hope you realize that we couldn't do it without you.
This is one of the Expedition's harvesters. Have they gone this far?
Catherina closed the world but it never stopped you. You found a way in.
You're here! How fortunate. First, the aborigines attacked, then the machines went mad, so I just ran... and ran, and ran. And then I found myself here. I'm stuck. Will you help me free?
I'm waiting for the right moment. Don't worry, I'll get the others. I'd rather land in woodfaces' prison than in the middle of the rise of the machines.
Uh, that's much better. Thanks. I'll find my own way from here when it gets quiet.
That's a thing to thank for! I should go to prison, you say? Oh, well then... I'm sure you'll think of something to let us out. I'll take a short breather and go.
Ugh, where are they? I can't go anywhere without my goggles.
Yes, yes. The prison. I remember. I'll be on my way soon. I don't want to rush to get to prison.
I've lost my goggles! Can you believe it? They should be here but I can't find them, I'm almost blind! Will you help?
I know! You're the messenger of the green people! Do they want me back in their prison? Alright. I know, they rule everything and everyone here.
And those who fail to obey them will suffer... the consequences. Why would they need our cows, though?
Do you think I'm a woman in need? Haven't you learned anything from Ferris? No way. I escaped to think through a rescue plan. And here's what I'm thinking...

You see, the green people are pacifists by nature, right? Aha. So they sent you to break down mechanoids. They don't want to do it with their own hands. That's also the reason why we all ended up in prison and not dead.

So, they're pacifists. This means...

...that they're easy to persuade to let us go. As... as goodwill ambassadors!

Honestly, I hate the whole idea of the stand between the Expedition and the Forestfolk. We're nothing but occupants on this land. We broke in, started tearing down the trees, pumping out ambrosia... I know it's for a good cause, but I deeply hate the approach.

And then you go on breaking the remaining mechanoids, and I'll go to prison. We must go apart, because you attract too much attention. I'll sneak quietly in the shadow. I'll see you there. And then we'll figure out what to do with the prisoners. Alright, chop-chop.
Stay away from my plans. Ciao!
Billions of years passed before my eyes...

Gah!

Don't get me wrong, I'm happy that we've found them. I hope they'll get in touch soon. But the Children... they won't let us to a thing on Eden. What are we going to do? We'll have to make a deal and exchange ambrosia for something. I wonder what they'd be interested in...

As to mechanoids, they're in defense state. They attack everything that seems hostile... which is pretty much everything around here. I must say, Ivan and Felix were outraged. You broke down a lot of very expensive machines. I'll try and justify your actions for them.

How curious. Another Nihaz's child? The goddess of Darkness and Death?

She's a very dangerous creature, threatening both us and All-Mother. We must convince the willful goddess to unite our forces against Nihaz's messengers.

I also wonder whom Hirkalla was talking about. What are the Sparks that came from Sarnaut to Eden? If the Sage is the Umoir god that, as you say, has left our world... then who is the Madman?

A Great Mage that we know nothing about? A new ancient god? If Klavdia didn't have Tep's Spark, I could think that it was him. But she's had it since the Pyramid.

Yes, our research.

The results are very curious.

As I said, the builders of this city were quite advanced. They mined metals, dug quarries.

The settlement was destroyed by someone else. It looks like an external attack. There are traces of strikes and repairs. It stopped helping at some point, though. They either left the city or all died.

I'll try to find out more. Return to All-Mother and try to make that deal.
What is the foundation of all things?
These are important elements, but they are not the foundation but the top.
That's right. Fire, water, air, and earth manifest themselves in many ways.
What? This is… some nonsense. Think again.
What is the Circle of Life?
That's right. Without death there is no life. Everything you see is interconnected and balanced. Everything serves what was before and what comes after. Everything is necessary.
I don't think you understand my question.
That's right. Death is part of the cycle, just like life. Everything you see is interconnected and balanced. Everything serves what was before and what comes after. Everything is necessary.
Let's proceed. What divine powers do you know?
A strange set of concepts. It seems that my lesson hasn't sunk in.
That's right. Tell me, why didn't I destroy the Darkness?
Yes, I didn't want to destroy it, but why?
That's right, darkness is as much a part of my design as everything else. Why do we consider Nihaz a rebel?
My strength is not about fighting. It's about being able to create. But Nihaz is no match for my children.
That's right. Nihaz did not want to perform his role and decided to destroy the Great Circle.
No, Darkness itself is necessary and not evil.
Sometimes I wonder about your sanity when you say things like that...
True, but what happens if someone takes too much?
True, but what happens if the connection is broken?
True, but what happens if the balance is upset?
True, but what if it doesn't happen?
What needs to be done to prevent this from happening?
What can we do to prevent it from coming?
Such a solution would eventually lead to disaster. But could life recover from it?
Well, that shows your indifference, but let's say we do that. Can a garden exist without a gardener?
If they fail, what will happen?
But would a garden exist without a gardener?
You don't believe in the power of life? That's unfortunate.
The gardener, of course, improves the garden, but the garden is not that weak on its own.
That's right. Life will find a way and correct all mistakes, but if we want our gardens to flourish, we need someone to maintain the balance.
No, life is stronger than this. It's much more powerful than it seems.
You named the divine forces and the forces of nature, but what is the name of the powers of the demiurges?
These sound like the heralds of doomsday, not the powers of the demiurges. Think again.
And that's right. What can you say about death?
No, that's not correct. What do demiurges have to do with those?
That's correct, even though they're usually named differently. What can you say about death?
No, these are not the powers of the demiurges. We will not talk about them now.
It looks like you don't understand my lessons!
That's right, but what are the forces of Destruction?
You have only violated divine laws. And this is not the Gift of Tensess, but the Gift of Nihaz!
Once you become truly immortal, you will lose life in its entirety.
This is the correct answer. But what can you say about Destruction?
That's right. But what can resist Time?
No, it's not. It's just one of the powers.
That's right, the circle is turning and Destruction is the fate of all worlds. But what opposes time?
Even the combined power of the gods cannot defeat time.
No, Nihaz wants to break the Great Circle itself, and Destruction is part of the Circle.
That's right. But how is Creation different from Life?
Nihaz can disturb a thin stream, but the river of time will sweep him away.
Life obeys time, though it fights against it, constantly losing.
No matter how strong Order is, unstoppable time will turn it into ruins.
True. But they create Life. What is the difference between Life and Creation?
No, Life and Creation are different things.
There is no conflict between Life and Creation, although they are not united.
And this is true. Creation is the beginning of history, and Life is history itself.
The answer here is unambiguous, and if you understand the essence of my lessons, you know it.
The truth is absolute. Think more about this question.
What do you know about heroes like you?
True. But who creates heroes and why?
True. But who creates heroes and why?
True. But who creates heroes and why?
No, heroes are created by gods, they are chosen by higher powers. But what should heroes do?
A hero comes at the call of the gods who have chosen them. But what is the hero's duty?
That's right, a hero is chosen by the gods. But what do we need a hero for?
Chosen by the gods, needed by their people. But why are they needed?
Who is that beautiful lady that your heart wants? But the truth is, the gods choose the hero, endowing them with a special destiny. But why?
Don't extraordinary circumstances indicate that the hero has been chosen by the gods? But what should such a chosen one do?
This is true, since such creatures threaten their people. But where do monsters come from?
Treasures are usually guarded by monsters. But where do those monsters come from?
But who threatens beautiful maidens if not monsters? Where do they come from?
What can the gods desire but for feats to be performed in their name? Feats require the presence of an enemy that you will fight, and where will this enemy come from?
The only way to become strong is to pass tests by slaying many monsters. But where would they come from?
What kind of a hero are they, then, if they don't perform feats? Their only task is to fight monsters that are a threat to people's lives. But where do monsters come from?
The truth is, monsters are needed for a hero to become a hero, and so they will indeed appear at some point. But what is the hero looking for at the end of their journey?
These powers often spawn monsters, especially Chaos. Monsters have always existed and will continue to exist, and there will always be a hero who defeats them. But what will the hero be looking for?
True, because where the hero has passed, monsters are no more. But what is the hero looking for?
Yes, this is the fate of all heroes - to fight monsters and perform feats. But what reward does the hero want at the end of their journey?
Yes, because civilizations are created by heroes who hunt monsters and move borders. But what are all the heroes looking for?
This is partly true, because there is no hero without monsters, and perhaps there are no monsters without a hero? What does a hero who defeats monsters want?

There are no treasures you can take with you to the realm of no return. Everything is meaningless in the face of death, and every hero, in the end, is looking for a way to avoid it. But do they find it?
A pointless and pathetic attempt. The laws of the gods are unbreakable, and mortals are unable to violate them. Only the immortal can challenge the gods. But will the hero find immortality?
Times are cruel, and whoever is beautiful today will wither tomorrow like a flower in fall. Only immortality can bestow infinite happiness, and every hero strives for it. But can they attain it?
Only a god can challenge a god, only an immortal can resist an immortal. The fate of mortals is bitter, and every hero is looking for ways to escape their fate. But can they?

Many people follow this path, trying to unravel the true meaning of my design. But a mortal cannot follow this path - they will fall before reaching the end. Only an immortal knows the secrets of the world. But can the hero find their immortality?
That's right. But can they find it?
There are no forces that can break the grip of death.
There are no troops capable of storming the realm from which there is no return.
There are no wise men who know how to escape a fate that is inevitable.
There is no such feat that is rewarded with this favor.
There are no words to soften a heart that has already passed judgment.
If you stop acting crazy and listen to me, you might change your mind about what's happening...

Don't want to be strung along anymore?

This ideal little world is not that simple at all... There was a lot going on here you weren't told about.

I saw your Catherina study the ruins of an "unknown ancient civilization"... What do you think happened to this ruined city?

Once upon a time there were travelers just like you. They built houses, looked for metals in the ground, cut down trees...

The All-Mother destroyed them all. No other alternative is acceptable to her. The same fate awaits you, if you listen blindly to her. Think about it.

Perhaps you've had enough of the gods? It's time to take fate into your own hands.

Do you want to fight Nihaz?

But do you really need to call on some goddess to help you? What do you personally think about it?

You have to decide.
Do you still not understand why they don't want to die?
They used to be the same as your new friends, but their Tree's lifespan has come to an end. Now they are doomed.
Cruel, senseless sentence - just like everything my mother does!
I extended their lives as best I could. But she? She could give them new ones. But she won't do that.
I opened their eyes, exposing the blatant injustice of what happened to them.
We're tired of waiting. I'll tell you everything, just be willing to listen...
Traitor! You are all traitors! How treacherous! How deceitful!

How foul...

We agreed that the harvesting of Ambrosia would be stopped! But your mechanoids started harvesting it in the Ambrosia Valley, a sacred place at the very roots of the Great Tree...

We are not going to tolerate this kind of insolence any longer. Our warriors are going into battle to throw you out of this world!

Your tribesmen cannot be trusted!

We agreed that the harvesting of Ambrosia would be stopped! But your mechanoids started harvesting it in the Ambrosia Valley, the sacred place at the very roots of the Great Tree...

We are not going to tolerate this kind of insolence any longer. Our warriors are going into battle to throw you out of this world!

Foul hypocrite! All this time, you and the others have been working for the Expedition!

We agreed that the harvesting of Ambrosia would be stopped! But your mechanoids started harvesting it in the Ambrosia Valley, the sacred place at the very roots of the Great Tree...

We are not going to tolerate this kind of insolence any longer. Our warriors are going into battle to throw you out of this world!

I don't know whose side you're on!

Go back to your tribe! Get out of my sight!
Then go to the Expedition's camp and deliver my message! Your tribesmen will answer for this betrayal!
Return to your tribesmen, you vile traitor! Get out of my sight!
Haven't we given you enough time? What have you been up to? Your task was to arrange for us to be allowed to harvest Ambrosia. What have you accomplished?

Making demands? I must have misheard.

What right do you have to demand anything from me? Perhaps you've become too attached to these aborigines? Do you want to be executed for treason?

Your task was to arrange for us to be allowed to harvest Ambrosia. What have you accomplished?

I'm tired of waiting. We're wasting time. How much longer do we have to wait for something to change?

These negotiations are a joke.

Your task was to arrange for us to be allowed to harvest Ambrosia. What have you accomplished?
Yes? Or maybe you got them to agree to help us in our fight against Nihaz? Is this All-Mother ready to join us?

That's what I'm talking about...

These gods are useless. They are nothing but trouble.

I'm tired of this. We'll solve our problems ourselves. If we can get enough Ambrosia, then we'll be as powerful as the gods.

From now on, anyone who stands in our way will be crushed. If the Children try to stop us, we will burn everything to the ground!

Now report back to Catherina about everything you've learned. I'm preparing a general offensive to protect our Harvesters.
How is it going? Not very well, I see...

I suspected it might end like this.

We have nothing to offer them. Advanced magical technology? Holy icons? Gibberling beer? They don't need any of this.

They won't back down and compromise.

Well, if we can’t come to an agreement, then it's going to be easy.

Well, if that really is the case, then we won't be able to negotiate with the goddess either.

Sorry, but I'm not ready to give up the comforts of civilization to wrap myself in leaves and live on a tree.

We have no other choice. To save Sarnaut, we need the Ambrosia.
I'm glad that you decided to give your heart to Eden. Help my Children. They're in dire need, for our world has never had to face an invasion.

I knew that you'd choose your own world. But I hope I managed to explain things to you. Your Expedition also needs your support, for Nihaz has long been obscuring your hearts. Come back for new lessons when you're ready.
